record.paper_title: The Feynman integral path a Henstock integral: a survey and open problems
record.context_brief: Extending the no-natural-Banach-norm result to H
record.original_question: For the function space H of Henstock-integrable functions on path space R^T, does the known theorem that there is no natural Banach space norm on Henstock integrable functions from R^n to R extend to H as well?

evidence.quote: in the case Rn, it is possible to show that there exists no natural Banach space norm on Henstock integrable functions over Rn to R, see [27, Theorem 2.7], which makes us think that this result can be extended over H

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T$ be a (possibly uncountable) index set and consider the path space $\mathbb{R}^T$ of all functions $\gamma : T \to \mathbb{R}$. Suppose that an appropriate notion of Henstock (Henstock–Kurzweil-type) integral has been defined on $\mathbb{R}^T$, and let $\mathcal{H}$ denote the corresponding linear space of Henstock-integrable real-valued functions on $\mathbb{R}^T$ (the space used to give a rigorous Henstock-integral formulation of the Feynman path integral).

It is known that for the finite-dimensional analogue — the space $HK(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathbb{R})$ of Henstock–Kurzweil integrable functions $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ — there exists no "natural" Banach space norm; that is, $HK(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathbb{R})$ cannot be equipped with a norm, defined intrinsically from the Henstock integration structure, that makes it a Banach space.

Question: Does this non-existence result extend to the path-space setting? More precisely, prove or disprove that there is no natural Banach space norm on $\mathcal{H}$, i.e. that $\mathcal{H}$ admits no intrinsic norm under which it becomes a Banach space.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches return results confirming the finite-dimensional fact (no natural Banach norm on HK(R^n,R)) and works that introduce alternative Fréchet/Banach structures for Feynman path integrals, but no source establishing or disproving the analogous statement for the Henstock-integrable function space on the path space R^T was found. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The topology of the space of HK integrable functions in R^n
status_evidence.snippet: HK(R^n) has no natural Banach norm; it is shown to be an uncountable union of Fréchet spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the finite-dimensional non-existence result that motivates the path-space question.

status_evidence.title: Banach Spaces for the Feynman Integral
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs alternative Banach spaces suitable for Feynman path integrals, in light of the lack of natural Banach norm on HK spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates ongoing work on functional-analytic frameworks for path integrals; the specific extension to H on R^T is not addressed.
